id: Wellington Lions 2026 Season-Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Wellington Lions 2026 Season
long_description:
Hnry Stadium has already hosted some memorable rugby moments in 2026, including Hurricanes and All Blacks victories. Now the Wellington Lions return for five home games as the NPC marks a major milestone.
The season begins with a Heritage Round clash against Hawke's Bay, celebrating the players and teams that have shaped Wellington rugby. Other home fixtures will feature themed match days, from club rugby celebrations to recognising local emergency services. With family-friendly kick-off times, entertainment, and ticket offers throughout the season, there's plenty happening both on and off the field.
On 19 and 27 September, one ticket delivers double the action as the Wellington Pride women's side join the Lions for double-header fixtures.
Whether you're a lifelong supporter or looking for a great day out, the NPC's 50th season is the perfect time to get behind the Lions and join the roar.

id: WOBIL: Wise Old Bugger in Lycra-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: WOBIL: Wise Old Bugger in Lycra
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
The last in a trilogy of cycling-themed plays skids into The Wellington Opera House in May.  Writer-director Gregory Cooper and seasoned Kiwi actor Mark Hadlow collaborate once more to bring their cycling trilogy to a close. The one-man play 'WOBIL: Wise Old Bugger in Lycra' follows previous installments ‘MAMIL: Middle Aged Man In Lycra’ and ‘GOMIL: Grumpy Old Man In Lycra’. Expect familiar faces, trademark physical comedy, plenty of laughs, and a fair bit of heart too.
Mark is one of New Zealand’s best-known actors. You might have seen him on screen in ‘King Kong’ or ‘The Hobbit’, or a host of live professional theatre shows on stages around the motu.  Gregory's past work includes ‘That Bloody Woman’. This latest chapter sends Wayne on his hardest hill climb yet. With help, and hindrance, from a few old friends and enemies, he’s determined to go out in a blaze of lycra glory. Get ready for one last spin through friendship, ageing, and resilience.

id: Menopause The Musical-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Menopause The Musical
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Described as the ultimate ladies’ night out, Menopause the Musical has been delivering laughs across the globe for years. Now the fun-filled musical about ‘the change’ returns to Wellington for one night.
Set in a department store, four women meet by chance while shopping for a black lace bra. Though they couldn’t be more different, they quickly discover a shared bond over memory loss, hot flushes, night sweats, and mood swings. What follows is a hilarious, heart-warming musical told with love, laughter and the greatest hits of the 60s, 70s and 80s. The laughter-filled 90-minute production gets audiences out of their seats dancing and singing along to clever parodies of beloved pop classics.
Winner of over 40 Tony Awards, Menopause the Musical has entertained more than 17 million fans worldwide. It’s been translated into nine languages and performed in more than 500 cities. The show’s enduring appeal lies in its honesty, hilarity and heart. It celebrates women everywhere and turns shared experiences into shared joy.

id: Abracadabra-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Abracadabra
venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Get ready for 60 dazzling minutes of magic at The Opera House. Anthony Street, one of the world's leading magicians and illusionists, takes you on a  spectacular journey you won't forget. Abracadabra will have you gasping in awe, laughing out loud, and gripping the edge of your seat.
Picture curtains rising to reveal impossible scenes, balls of fire, and a giant bouncy ball launching into the crowd. Volunteers are plucked from the audience and find themselves part of the act. Every moment is built to thrill kids and grown-ups alike. These are the kind of surprises that will have you asking — "how did he do that?" All ages are welcome, from first-time magic fans to adults who still cannot figure out how it is done.

id: Home Brew presents Last Week-Shed 6, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Home Brew presents Last Week
long_description:
Home Brew's legendary 'Last Week' EP has come of age and it's coming to the capital to celebrate. Released 18 years ago, 'Last Week' follows seven days in the life of roguish hip-hop crew Home Brew.
The group built a devoted following through a string of independent releases in the early 2010s. Its self-titled debut album in 2012 reached number one in New Zealand. The group returned to the charts in 2023 with 'Run It Back', introducing its music to a new generation of listeners.
The group will play 'Last Week' in full at Shed 6, alongside favourites from its celebrated catalogue. Known for a DIY approach and uncompromising sound, Home Brew remains one of the country's most celebrated hip-hop acts. The show offers Wellington fans the chance to revisit a landmark release and hear the songs that have shaped the group's enduring legacy.

id: System Of A Down-Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: System Of A Down
long_description:
Following the sell-out success of their European summer tour, System Of A Down is heading to Hnry Stadium for its only New Zealand concert. Wellington audiences will also be entertained by warm up act and alternative rock icons Faith No More. 
This concert marks System of a Down's first Wellington show, and their first time playing in Aotearoa in more than a decade. Blending metal with diverse influences including jazz, opera, and Armenian folk, System Of A Down have sold more than 42 million albums worldwide. They released their debut self-titled album in 1998, but it was not until the release of 'Toxicity' in 2001 that their popularity exploded. Heavy music fans can expect a massive career-spanning set filled with the songs that have defined the genre for more than 25 years.
It's been a long time between Wellington shows for Faith No More. The last time the San Francisco-based band played in the capital was 1997. Responsible for such classics as Epic, Midlife Crisis, and a distinctive cover of The Commodores' Easy, they've developed a die-hard following over the last 40 years. 
Together the bands will bring decades of hard rock (and its fans) to Wellington for what promises to be one of the most electrifying nights of heavy music the city's ever seen.
